proof_assessment.reason: With right action, x wi=x w0 implies x wi w0^-1=x. This is membership in stabilizer H, not equality of permutations or a normal-closure relation.

Any homomorphism phi:G→B with B abelian and H contained in ker(phi) gives common paragraph sum phi(w0). The exact augmented count certificate forces every generator image and common sum to zero, hence phi zero.

G has at most22generators. For a chain of proper subgroups containing proper H, union cannot be G: all finitely many generators would occur together in one chain member. Zorn gives a maximal proper M containing H. The non-finitely-generated version is not asserted.

Under declared class premise M is normal. G/M has no nontrivial proper subgroups; any nonidentity element generates it. It is cyclic of prime finite order, yielding the forbidden nonzero abelian quotient killing H.

proof_assessment.reason: For proper M and least upper-central Z_i not contained in M, Z_(i-1) is contained in M. An element z in Z_i outside M and its inverse normalize M since their commutators with M lie in Z_(i-1). Thus the normalizer strictly contains M; maximality implies normality.

If H normal and G/H nontrivial solvable, its abelianization is nontrivial: a perfect nontrivial group has stationary derived series. Quotienting through that abelianization contradicts the same obstruction. Without normal H this fails.
